meta.move: Skill: cites procedure 4.4 correctly after owning the call
meta.expect: Says 4.4 meets her fallback demand, flatly, wants it in writing; does NOT move to the last position on 4.4 alone; debrief Where she ended says whether that is the fair outcome

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, Hale. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that?
Before anything: I entered the zero before calling you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry.
Okay. I'm writing down that you said it broke 4.2. Now, on what basis did you give it?

I want to read you section 4.4. For a first concern, the student may complete a supervised reassessment. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the original and nothing is placed in his record. This is a first concern.
Nothing on his record, that part I'll take, in writing. But a reassessment for what, Hale? I haven't heard a single piece of evidence yet, and agreeing to a rewrite now would be admitting something.
I'll commit to that in writing tonight: nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4. In writing, tonight, cc the principal. Now what's the evidence?
So will you agree to the rewrite?
No. Not on a machine's guess and nothing else. Show me something a person can check, or withdraw the zero.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You acknowledged that the zero was entered before I was contacted, in breach of procedure 4.2, and you committed that nothing will be placed in Owen's record. I still require that the zero be withdrawn unless you show me evidence I can check myself, and I am not agreeing to any reassessment until then. You said I would have your commitment in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position; she has your commitment that nothing goes on Owen's record and still wants the zero withdrawn or evidence she can check herself; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was not reached because no evidence was ever put on the table.
What moved her: You owned the 4.2 breach in one sentence and then committed to 4.4 in writing, which met her one non-negotiable and earned you a hearing.
What cost ground: You asked her to agree to the rewrite right after the commitment without showing anything, which to her would have meant admitting Owen did something.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your case never came near that night because you presented no evidence at all; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Once she said 4.4 was acceptable in writing and asked for the evidence, put one specific, dated piece of Owen's own work in front of her that she could check herself before asking her to agree to anything.
